title: Upper Lower Light/Heavy 4 days split with mirror Week program review (part. 1)
summary: Part one of a review of Joel's 4-day upper/lower program with week A/B mirror weeks and light and heavy days. NH approves the A/B structure and conventional deadlifts but rejects light/heavy days for bodybuilding, calling 4x10 light work junk volume. He says to do both exercises instead of rotating unequal ones within a day, and suggests supersets, end-of-set shrugs and repositioning strength work within a session.
claims: A week A/week B system working the same muscles with different exercises suits advanced intermediates and people who like variety
A/B days don't have to follow each other in strict order
Overhead press 4x4-6 is a good range; since it's a safe lift you can even do 1-2 rep maxes
Weighted pull-ups 4x4-6 is a good range
Don't rotate a compound with an isolation in the same slot (close-grip bench vs skull crushers); they aren't equivalent and wreck tonnage tracking
Do both close-grip bench and skull crushers as a zero-rest superset; it won't hurt strength or recovery
Close-grip bench is a low-impact press you can hardly overdo
Skull crushers should be 4x8-12, not 4-6, focusing on the stretch and negative
Curls and lateral raises at 3x8-10 are excellent; small isolation lifts don't need rotating, just do them all as a giant set
Supersetting two rear delt isolations is too much for a small muscle; modify the face pull toward the traps instead
He dislikes light and heavy days for bodybuilding; ramping up is only for returning from injury or sickness (e.g. 245 instead of 300 lb)
Bodybuilders need strength stability: you should never deadlift 40 lb less than last session
RDLs suit a 4x8-12 window because they quickly enter dangerous territory for muscle strains
Heavy back squats followed by RDLs is a match made in heaven; a light squat day plus leg press wastes time
Hamstring curls beat leg extensions for injury prevention and development because they provide a stretch
Superset calves with hamstring curls; a lone set of calves wastes time
RDLs can be supersetted with pull-ups; finish every pull with shrugs at the end of the set until you can't shrug strictly
Paused bench is an excellent bodybuilding exercise, not just for powerlifting
Light 4x10 squats or 4x10-12 bench are junk volume in an irrelevant intensity window; use a range that takes you near failure or deliberate RIR
If you must keep a lighter bench, do one heavy set with 3 RIR to keep stimulus without digging into reserves
Rather than light bench then dumbbell press, make the dumbbell press the strength work
Incline dumbbell press can be supersetted with incline chest-supported rows for upper back at no time cost
Always open with strength work; a second strength lift can be repositioned later in the session, after other body parts, to recover
Deadlift 3x3 is medium volume, high intensity, with some sandbagging; good range
Barbell rows after deadlifts start with a pre-fatigued lower back, which can be dangerous for some
After your last barbell row, stand up and shrug the bar; the pre-fatigued traps get an intense weighted stretch
Lat pulldown handles should be directly overhead; adjust torso angle and don't pull with only the arms
Use a flexible 1-3 sets of 3 on deadlifts and 3-4x8-12 on rows to manipulate intensity
exercises: upper back work at no time cost
stand up after last rep and shrug
handles directly overhead, adjust torso angle
